summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require warning labels for regulated imported food, covering packaged imports and unpackaged or minimally packaged food displayed for retail sale.
The prescribed warning would identify food as imported and state that Australian growing or processing standards had not been followed and health harm was possible.
Labelling duties and related offences would begin six months after Royal Assent, while the remaining provisions would begin the day after Royal Assent.
changes: Importing regulated packaged food without the warning would attract a $500,000 penalty.
Retail operators displaying regulated unpackaged food without the warning would face a $500,000 penalty.
Retail operators displaying regulated minimally packaged food without the warning would face a $500,000 penalty.
Unpackaged food warnings could be attached to the item or displayed prominently nearby.
Rules could prescribe label size and other display requirements.
summary.affected: Importers of regulated packaged food, operators of regulated retail food businesses and consumers buying imported food are affected.
